newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat ends mostly lower on commission selling.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat ends mostly lower on commission selling.

text.p: CBOT wheat futures closed mostly lower with nearby contracts under pressure from late commission house selling, pit traders said.
O'Connor and Co sold 700,000 bushels of March near the close, pit sources said. In other late trade, locals were noted short covering and Cargill Inc bought 300 lots of July, traders said.

Traders said selling was tied to ideas farmer sales would pick up after the first of the year. Many farmers had been holding onto grain to defer tax payments until next year and were expected to sell in January.
News that Pakistan would tender next month for 270,000 tonnes U.S. and Australian wheat was supportive, as were rumors Brazil was looking to buy 500,000 tonnes Argentine wheat, pit sources said.

Ideas of increased export demand erased pessimism from Friday's USDA export inspections. The tally for the week ended December 26 totalled 4.5 million bushels, the lowest since 1982 when USDA began keeping computerized records.
Wheat closed two cents per bushel higher to 3/4 cents lower with March down 3/4 at $3.81-1/4. The market will be closed Wednesday in observance of the New Year's Day holiday.
Volume was estimated at 6,000 contracts, compared with Monday's actual volume of 10,271 contracts.
